documentNotes.title: Instructions
documentNotes.statement:
(Read completely before you begin)

This is the second round qualification test for the USAAAO team. The test is short answer, consisting of 12 short questions and 2 longer, multipart questions. Once you begin, you will have two and a half hours (150 minutes) to complete the test. You may use the provided table of constants and a scientific calculator. No other materials are permitted.

Please show all your work. Answers without work will not receive credit. You will need to write your solutions on a separate sheet. Please begin a new page for each question, and number your pages. Please write as clearly as possible. Your test will be scanned for grading, so make sure that your writing is dark enough to be legible once scanned.

When you are done, please have your teacher scan your work and send it to usioaateam@gmail.com. We prefer to receive your work as a single pdf, named lastname_firstname.pdf.

Good luck.

transcription.notes: The paper prints 12 short problems („Short Problems“, Problem 1–12) and 2 long problems („Long Problems“, Long Problem 1–2); they are numbered 1–14 here, with Long Problem 1 and 2 as problems 13 and 14. No total is printed (6×12 + 30 + 37 = 139); the long-problem parts add up to the printed 30 and 37. There is no solutions document in the archive, so every solution is marked incomplete and no answers are given. The star table of Long Problem 1 is a raster image on page 4 and is transcribed as a Markdown table. Printed forms kept verbatim: „the Earths surface“ (missing apostrophe, Problem 8); „$M_bol$“ with only the b subscripted (Problem 9); „The coordinates of Jakarta, Indonesia is“ (agreement error kept as printed per D-P28, Long Problem 1 b.); „degrees East .“ with a space before the period (Long Problem 1 b.); „estimate the ate at $z_{eq}$“ („ate“ is presumably „age“, but it is a real word, so kept, Long Problem 2 d.); „Assuming $\Omega_{CMB} = 0.3$“ (presumably $\Omega_m$, kept as printed, Long Problem 2 c.); the unfinished sentence „Assuming the temperature … $gcm^{-3}$.“ of Long Problem 2 is kept as printed. The non-word „gien“ in Long Problem 2 is corrected to „given“ and recorded in tx.edits.

problems.title: Long Problem 1
problems.statement:
Use the given table to answer the following questions.

| Star | Right Ascension | Declination |
|---|---|---|
| Aldebaran | $4^{\mathrm{h}}\,36^{\mathrm{m}}$ | $16^{\circ}\,31'$ |
| Miaplacidus | $9^{\mathrm{h}}\,13^{\mathrm{m}}$ | $-69^{\circ}\,42'$ |
| Deneb | $20^{\mathrm{h}}\,41^{\mathrm{m}}$ | $45^{\circ}\,20'$ |
| Regulus | $10^{\mathrm{h}}\,08^{\mathrm{m}}$ | $12^{\circ}\,18'$ |
| Hadar | $14^{\mathrm{h}}\,04^{\mathrm{m}}$ | $-60^{\circ}\,24'$ |

parts.label: a.
parts.statement: If the star Deneb crosses your local meridian, how long must you wait until Miaplacidus crosses your local meridian?

parts.label: b.
parts.statement: The coordinates of Jakarta, Indonesia is 6.17 degrees South and 106.82 degrees East . Which of these stars would never be visible to an observer in Jakarta?

parts.label: c.
parts.statement: At the instant Miaplacidus crosses the local meridian of an observer in Jakarta, what is its altitude and azimuth?

parts.label: d.
parts.statement: At the instant Miaplacidus crosses the local meridian of an observer in Jakarta, what is the latitude and longitude of an observer who will see Aldebaran at the zenith?

parts.label: e.
parts.statement: For an observer at Jakarta, how long will Aldebaran be above the horizon, from sunset to sunrise?

parts.label: f.
parts.statement: What is the angular separation between Regulus and Hadar?

parts.label: g.
parts.statement: When Aldebaran is rising, what is the altitude of Miaplacidus as seen by an observer in Jakarta?

solution.incompleteReason: No solutions file in the archive

problems.title: Long Problem 2
problems.statement: The energy density of blackbody radiation is given by $u = 4\sigma T^4/c$, where $\sigma$ is the Stefan-Boltzmann constant. Assuming the temperature of the CMB today is $T_{CMB} = 2.73K$ and the critical density today is $\rho_{crit} = 0.921 * 10^{-29} h_{70}^2 g cm^{-3}$.

parts.label: a.
parts.statement: What is the energy density of the CMB? What is the corresponding $\Omega_{CMB}$?

parts.label: b.
parts.statement: What are the typical photon energies of the CMB, and the corresponding number density of photons per $cm^3$?

parts.label: c.
parts.statement: Assuming $\Omega_{CMB} = 0.3$ what was the redshift $z_{eq}$ of the transition from the radiation dominated to the matter dominated universe?

parts.label: d.
parts.statement: Assuming the age of the universe at the epoch of decoupling to be 380,000 years, and knowing its redshift, estimate the ate at $z_{eq}$. You can assume the expansion laws appropriate for an $\Omega = 1$ universe.

parts.label: e.
parts.statement: How old was the universe at the time when the temperature was comparable to the temperature in the Solar core, $T_c = 1.5 * 10^7 K$?

parts.label: f.
parts.statement: What were typical photon energies then?
